,,fently enjoy moft freely. Which , though every Patron
,,ought proportionably to doe, yet the horrible corruptions
,,abroad in the world in fuch cafes, do (as it were) by a kind
,,of Antiperiftafis make a duty a tranfcendent vertue. And
,,this was not all. Though incrochments upon te Church be
,,like the breaches of the fea;a thoufand to one never returne:
,,yet did he restore to a farthing all that;which had a long ti-
,,me beene detain'd from the Church ; and parted with it
,,moft freely; though he had as much wit and power as any
,,other to have continued it so , ifhe had pleas'd. And I faid
,,Ecclefiafticall Livings, though I inftance but in one ; becaufe
,,I partly knew his purpofe for the reft. For , he gave me
,,himfelfe this meffage to as worthy and reverend a man, as
,,Iknow unprefer'd in this Land;that is he would come unto
,,him , hee would give him the firft that fell ; and for no ot-
,,her reafon in the world, but becaufe he heard he was a re-
,,verend and worthy man. Now lay thefe things to the pra-
,,ctice of the times, wherein there is fuch finfull ad Simonia-
,,call packing together, compacting, fecret convenanting
,,with the party or friends for prefent money, or after grati-
,,fications : fome part of the tithes , or his owne muft be re-
,,ferv'd to the Patron, or he muft be the Farmer at his owne
,,price; or pin a wife upon the fleeve of the Parfon , as they
,,contemptuoufly fpeake, (abafe alfo and unworthy refpect)
,,or the like fuch wretched combinations to helpe one ano-
,,ther towards hell : my difacquaintance muft excufe my ig-
,,norance in the termes:and then tell me if this was not a no-
,,ble part in him worthy the imitation of the beft. I am per-
,,fwaded in this Point, he might be a patterne not onely to
,,all here prefent whom it might concerne, (though I looke
